title: Constructing the determinant norm from a principal free cover
statement:
Let $R,D$ be commutative rings, $\rho:R\to D$ unital, $r\ge0$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in R$ generate the unit ideal. Regard $D$ as an $R$-algebra through $\rho$. Suppose each $D_{f_i}$ is free with a basis of $r$ elements over $R_{f_i}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For $u\in D$ let $\mu_u$ be multiplication by $u$, and let $\chi_u(Z)\in R[Z]$ be its unique scalar-extension characteristic polynomial of [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence]. Then
$$N_{D/R}:D\to R,\qquad N_{D/R}(u)=(-1)^r\chi_u(0)$$
is the unique function with the following local determinant characterization: for every $a\in R$, every finite basis $e$ of $D_a$ over $R_a$, and $u\in D$, its image in $R_a$ is the determinant of multiplication by $u/1$ in $e$ [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. More generally, for every unital ring map $R\to R'$ making $D\otimes_R R'$ free with an $r$-element basis $e$, the image of $N_{D/R}(u)$ equals $\det(\mu_u\otimes1)$ in that basis [def-weil-module-base-change]. Thus the function is independent of the generating cover and all bases. If $p:\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is the associated map and $p_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}D}$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] (here $(p_*\mathcal O)(W)=\mathcal O(p^{-1}W)$), then for every affine open $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ on which $\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O)$ is finite free over $\mathcal O(V)$, the restriction of $N_{D/R}(u)$ equals the determinant of multiplication by $u|_{p^{-1}V}$, in every finite basis. Zero rings, $r=0$, and the empty cover when $R=0$ are included.

proof.text: For each $u\in D$, multiplication $\mu_u(d)=ud$ is $R$-linear, since $D$ is a commutative $R$-algebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] to this endomorphism and the given principal cover and rank-$r$ bases. Denote its unique polynomial by $\chi_u$ and set $N(u)=(-1)^r\chi_u(0)$. This defines a function on all of $D$, with no choice of a global basis.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:R\to S$ be unital and $e$ an $r$-element basis of $D\otimes_RS$. The scalar-extension characterization in [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] gives $\alpha(\chi_u)=\det(ZI_r-M_e)$, where $M_e$ is the matrix of $\mu_u\otimes1$. Evaluating at zero commutes with $\alpha$. The permutation formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] gives $\det(-M_e)=(-1)^r\det(M_e)$ by taking one minus sign out of each of the $r$ factors in every summand. Therefore $\alpha(N(u))=(-1)^{2r}\det(M_e)=\det(M_e)$. This calculation includes empty matrices and zero coefficient rings.

proof.text: In fact the equality in step 2 holds for any finite basis $e$ of $D\otimes_RS$, say of size $k$. Put $g_i=\alpha(f_i)$ and $T_i=S_{g_i}$. Applying $\alpha$ to a relation $\sum c_if_i=1$ shows that the $g_i$ generate the unit ideal. Over $T_i$ there is an $r$-element basis: extend the given basis over $R_{f_i}$ along $R_{f_i}\to T_i$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-transitive]. The basis $e$ also extends to a $k$-element basis over $T_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties](d). If $T_i\ne0$, the two coordinate isomorphisms give $T_i^k\simeq T_i^r$, so [lem-sfb-commutative-ring-invariant-basis-number] gives $k=r$; step 2 applies in that basis. If $T_i=0$, both elements being compared are its unique element. The localized matrix of multiplication is the entrywise image of $M_e$ by the same free-module properties; the permutation formula shows that taking its determinant commutes with $S\to T_i$. Consequently $\alpha(N(u))-\det(M_e)$ maps to zero in every $T_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-covering-glue](i) over $S$ to conclude equality in $S$.

proof.text: For $S=R_a$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] identifies $D\otimes_RR_a$ with $D_a$, carrying $d\otimes(b/a^q)$ to $bd/a^q$ and $\mu_u\otimes1$ to multiplication by $u/1$. Thus step 3 gives the required equality in every finite basis of $D_a$. If $N'$ is another function with this localization characterization, apply it at each $a=f_i$ in the given rank-$r$ basis. For every $u$, the element $N'(u)-N(u)$ has zero image in all $R_{f_i}$, hence is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-covering-glue](i). This proves uniqueness. The characterization quantifies over all $a$ and all finite bases and contains no chosen generating cover, so uniqueness also proves independence of the cover and the bases.

proof.text: For the affine-open assertion put $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $F=p_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}D}$ and $A=\mathcal O_X(V)$. Here $F(W)=\mathcal O(p^{-1}W)$, so $F(X)=D$. By hypothesis $F$ is quasi-coherent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to the open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, the affine opens $X$ and $V$, and $F$. The unit-compatible isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] identifies pullback along $j$ with restriction and the pullback unit with the ordinary restriction of sections. The stated unit-normalized map therefore gives the $A$-linear isomorphism $c:D\otimes_RA\to F(V)$, $d\otimes a\mapsto a(d|_{p^{-1}V})$. Under $c$, scalar extension of $\mu_u$ becomes multiplication by $u|_{p^{-1}V}$: on a pure tensor both composites have value $a((ud)|_{p^{-1}V})=u|_{p^{-1}V}\,a(d|_{p^{-1}V})$. Pure tensors generate, so the maps agree. Transport any given finite basis of $F(V)$ by $c^{-1}$ and apply step 3 with $S=A$. The corresponding multiplication matrices have identical entries. This proves the affine-open determinant formula in every finite basis.

proof.text: If $R=0$, unitality forces $D=0$; every unital scalar extension also has zero coefficient ring, and all asserted equalities and uniqueness hold in a singleton. This includes the empty generating cover: its span is the zero ideal, so it generates the unit ideal only when $R=0$. If $r=0$, the polynomial shape in [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] is $\chi_u=1$, so $N(u)=1_R$, agreeing with the empty determinant of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. All arguments above allow zero localizations; step 3 invoked invariant basis number only for the nonzero ones.

lean.statement: theorem principalFreeNorm_spec {R : Type u} {D : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing D] [Algebra R D] {r m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → R) (hgen : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) (hfree : ∀ i : Fin m, ∃ _e : Module.Basis (Fin r) (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) D), True) : (∀ (a : R) (k : ℕ) (e : Module.Basis (Fin k) (Localization.Away a) (LocalizedModule.Away a D)) (u : D), algebraMap R (Localization.Away a) (principalFreeNorm f hgen hfree u) = (LinearMap.toMatrix e e (localizedMul a u)).det) ∧ (∀ N : D → R, (∀ (a : R) (k : ℕ) (e : Module.Basis (Fin k) (Localization.Away a) (LocalizedModule.Away a D)) (u : D), algebraMap R (Localization.Away a) (N u) = (LinearMap.toMatrix e e (localizedMul a u)).det) → N = principalFreeNorm f hgen hfree) ∧ (∀ (S : Type (max u w)) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (e : Module.Basis (Fin r) S (S ⊗[R] D)) (u : D), algebraMap R S (principalFreeNorm f hgen hfree u) = (LinearMap.toMatrix e e ((LinearMap.mul R D u).baseChange S)).det)
lean.note: The norm is defined by the existing Algebra.locallyFreeCharpoly; the main theorem gives local characterization, uniqueness and scalar extension, and the companion theorem gives the affine-open clause. Added the already landed characteristic-polynomial definition node to stmt_deps.
